pill.desc: clear, colorless to slightly brown solution in a single-dose vial

tell: An amyloid-directed antibody with a terminal half-life of about 12 days, given as an infusion every four weeks.

clues.text: It is expected to be broken down by proteolytic enzymes, as endogenous IgG is, rather than cleared by the kidney or liver.
Produced in a Chinese hamster ovary cell line and supplied as a sterile, preservative-free solution.
Approved under a BLA as 350 mg single-dose vials, given as an infusion every four weeks.
Boxed warning for imaging abnormalities with edema and with hemosiderin deposition, which can be fatal. Contraindicated in known serious hypersensitivity.
Alzheimer's disease, with treatment started at the mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia stage.
Binds insoluble N-truncated pyroglutamate amyloid beta, which reduces amyloid plaques in the brain.
The generic name begins with D and has nine letters.
